lesson.title: Drugs Reviewer Framework
lesson.summary: Teach the reviewer how to reason about drugs across reference, use, possession, distribution, promotion, context and exceptions without collapsing all drug-related material into one concept.
learningObjectives: Distinguish drug reference from actual drug use.
Distinguish medical, educational and historical discussion from promotional or instructive content.
Recognize the difference between possession, sale, trafficking, manufacture and cultivation.
Recognize how context changes the meaning of drug-related evidence.
Assign confidence based on evidence strength and context stability.

concepts.title: Drug Reference
concepts.summary: Any explicit mention of drugs or narcotics.

concepts.title: Drug Consumption
concepts.summary: Use or intake of a drug by a person.

concepts.title: Drug Possession
concepts.summary: Having drugs on one’s person, in a vehicle or under control.

concepts.title: Drug Distribution
concepts.summary: Passing drugs from one person to another.

concepts.title: Drug Sale
concepts.summary: Commercial exchange of drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Purchase
concepts.summary: Buying drugs or arranging a buy.

concepts.title: Drug Smuggling
concepts.summary: Moving drugs illegally across borders or checkpoints.

concepts.title: Drug Trafficking
concepts.summary: Organized transport, trade or distribution of drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Manufacturing
concepts.summary: Producing, mixing or preparing drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Cultivation
concepts.summary: Growing or harvesting drug-producing plants.

concepts.title: Drug Storage
concepts.summary: Keeping drugs hidden, stored or cached.

concepts.title: Drug Transportation
concepts.summary: Moving drugs from one place to another.

concepts.title: Drug Glorification
concepts.summary: Treating drug activity as admirable or aspirational.

concepts.title: Drug Encouragement
concepts.summary: Urging another person to use or obtain drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Instruction
concepts.summary: Explaining how to use, make, hide or distribute drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Normalization
concepts.summary: Presenting drug activity as routine or harmless without clear context.

concepts.title: Drug Dependency
concepts.summary: Dependence or compulsion connected to drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Addiction
concepts.summary: Compulsive drug use with dependency or harm.

concepts.title: Drug Overdose
concepts.summary: Excessive ingestion or toxic drug reaction.

concepts.title: Drug Rehabilitation
concepts.summary: Treatment or recovery from drug dependency or misuse.

concepts.title: Medical Drug Use
concepts.summary: Approved or clinical drug use for treatment.

concepts.title: Prescription Drug Use
concepts.summary: Use of prescribed drugs according to medical direction.

concepts.title: Illegal Prescription Use
concepts.summary: Misuse, diversion or abuse of prescription drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Documentary
concepts.summary: Documentary narration or reporting about drugs.

concepts.title: Drug Educational
concepts.summary: Teaching or explaining drugs for education.

concepts.title: Drug Historical
concepts.summary: Historical reference to drugs or drug trade.

concepts.title: Drug News
concepts.summary: News reporting about drugs, raids or drug events.

concepts.title: Drug Comedy
concepts.summary: Humor or comic treatment of drug-related material.

concepts.title: Drug Satire
concepts.summary: Satirical treatment of drug activity.

concepts.title: Drug Dream
concepts.summary: Drug-related material occurring in a dream or dreamlike scene.

concepts.title: Drug Flashback
concepts.summary: Drug-related material in a flashback or memory.

concepts.title: Drug Hallucination
concepts.summary: Hallucinated or imagined drug-related material.

concepts.title: Drug False Accusation
concepts.summary: An accusation of drugs that is not supported by evidence.

concepts.title: Drug Symbolism
concepts.summary: Symbolic or metaphorical drug references.

concepts.title: Drug Scene Description
concepts.summary: Narrative scene description involving drug-related evidence.

concepts.title: Drug Dialogue
concepts.summary: Drug-related evidence delivered in dialogue.

concepts.title: Drug Implied Use
concepts.summary: Drug use implied by surrounding context rather than directly stated.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Identify whether the mention is a drug reference or a stronger drug concept.
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Start with the exact words and then classify the surrounding meaning.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Check whether the scene is medical, educational, historical, documentary or promotional.
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Do not assume a violation if the content is clearly contextual or instructional.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Check whether the evidence shows possession, use, sale, trafficking or manufacture.
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Choose the narrowest concept that the evidence actually supports.
evidenceRequirements: Explicit actions or implied actions supported by context.
Target and speaker identity where relevant.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Evaluate whether context changes the meaning of the drug-related statement.
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Context can reduce or increase reviewer confidence.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Determine whether the material is instructional or promotional.
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Promotion and instruction must not be inferred unless the scene supports them.

examples: The character says he is taking medication prescribed by a doctor.
The dialogue mentions drugs in a police report.
The scene shows a dealer handing a packet to another character.
counterExamples: A historical lecture mentioning narcotics is automatically a violation.
A medical discussion about prescription drugs is treated as glorification.
A joke about drugs is always treated as drug use.
exceptions: Comedy or satire when the meaning is clearly non-literal.
Dream, flashback or hallucination when the scene is not literal.

minimum: Exact drug-related words in the screenplay.
strong: Dialogue plus action or object evidence.
insufficient: Guessing drug intent from a single word.
Treating symbolic language as literal use without context.
confidenceGuidance: 100: Explicit drug evidence with strong context.
65: Evidence is present but interpretation needs caution.

conceptRelationships.note: A reference may support consumption if context shows use.
Repeated use may support addiction when the story confirms dependence.
Sale can be part of trafficking but not every sale is trafficking.
Medical guidance may clarify lawful prescription use.

reportTemplates.recommendationTemplate: Review the scene, speaker and intent before finalizing the finding.
